description:
A search query against a Synapse SearchIndex. The body of the request is the OpenSearch query DSL (the same shape OpenSearch's POST /{index}/_search accepts), allowlist-validated server-side and submitted to AOSS. The opaque query, aggregations, and suggest payloads are pass-through; the typed returnFields / sort / offset / limit / searchAfter properties are Synapse-specific concerns layered on top.

Field references use column names in every shape (DSL clauses, aggregation field, suggester field, sort, returnFields). The server resolves names to internal column ids before sending to OpenSearch, and rewrites them back to column names on response so callers see their original schema.

One of query or searchAfter is required. An empty request (neither set) is rejected with HTTP 400.

query.description:
An OpenSearch query DSL clause — the contents of the query key. Supports compound (bool / dis_max / constant_score / boosting) and leaf (match / multi_match / match_phrase / match_phrase_prefix / match_bool_prefix / term / terms / range / exists / prefix / wildcard / fuzzy / ids / simple_query_string / match_all) clauses. The server wraps the supplied subtree as a must clause inside its own bool so future server-side filter clauses can layer on without re-architecting.

Disallowed: script, script_score, function_score, more_like_this, geo_shape/shape with an indexed shape, has_child/has_parent, terms-lookup form, percolate, wrapper. Embedded script or indexed_shape anywhere in the subtree is rejected. Depth and total-clause caps bound query cost.

Example — full-text on the title column with a filter on year:

"query": {
  "bool": {
    "must":   [ { "match":  { "title": "amyloid" } } ],
    "filter": [ { "range":  { "year":  { "gte": 2010 } } } ]
  }
}

aggregations.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch aggregations object — the contents of the aggregations (or aggs) key, a map of aggregation name to definition. Supports terms / histogram / date_histogram / range / date_range / min / max / avg / sum / stats / extended_stats / value_count / cardinality / missing, with nested sub-aggregations.

Disallowed: scripted aggregations, pipeline aggregations, embedded script. Depth and per-request count caps bound cost.

Field references use column names. The raw aggregation result is returned as a JSON string on SearchQueryResults.aggregationResults with field references rewritten back to column names.

Example — one terms-by-year bucket count plus a top average score:

"aggregations": {
  "by_year":   { "terms": { "field": "year" } },
  "avg_score": { "avg":   { "field": "score" } }
}

suggest.description:
Optional. An OpenSearch suggesters object — the contents of the suggest key (a map of suggestion name to suggester definition, optionally alongside a top-level text). Returns query-assistance suggestions (did-you-mean / completion) as a JSON string in SearchQueryResults.suggestResults.

Allowlisted suggester types only: term, phrase, completion. Other suggesters and any embedded script (e.g. a phrase collate script) are rejected.

Field references use column names; results come back with the field reference reported as the column name.

Example — did-you-mean over the title column:

"suggest": {
  "did_you_mean": { "text": "amiloid", "term": { "field": "title" } }
}

searchAfter.description: Opaque cursor for deep pagination. Pass back the nextSearchAfter value returned by the previous page to retrieve the next page; cursors are stable as long as the underlying sort is unchanged. Mutually exclusive with offset — when supplied, the server pins from=0 and uses search_after. The cursor escapes the ~10,000-row offset window for browse / export.

returnFields.description: Columns to include in each hit's field list. Empty or null returns every indexed column on the matched documents. Narrowing this to the columns the caller actually displays reduces response size and transport cost, especially for wide SearchIndexes.

sort.description: Result ordering. Each entry specifies a column name (or the special '_score' pseudo-column, which sorts by relevance) and an ASC/DESC direction. When omitted, results are sorted by relevance descending (_score DESC). Sort columns must be stored as keyword or numeric sub-fields — for text columns this is handled automatically by routing through the keyword sub-field.

offset.description: Zero-based pagination offset into the hit list. Default: 0. Maximum: ~10,000 (the OpenSearch from + size ceiling). For deeper pagination use searchAfter.

limit.description: Maximum number of hits to return per page. Default: 25. Maximum: 100 (larger values are silently capped). Set to 0 in combination with FACETS-only response parts to retrieve only aggregation counts.
